title: Allocation System Instances are addressed by a chain, then protocol, then asset key rather than a flat list
content:
Most Primitives in the Pattern Artifact keep a flat Active Instances Directory. The Allocation System Primitive does not: A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.1.2 contains a chain level (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.1.2.1 - Ethereum Mainnet), which contains a protocol level (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.1.2.1.1 - Maple), which contains the pointer to a specific Instance Configuration Document named "Ethereum Mainnet - Maple USDC" (A.6.1.1.6.2.6.1.1.2.1.1.1).

The three-level key is a direct consequence of what the Primitive does. Capital allocation is inherently many-to-many — the same Agent may run several positions, in several protocols, on several chains, in several assets, all simultaneously and all with different terms. A flat directory would force every distinguishing fact into the instance name; the nested one makes chain and protocol into navigable dimensions.

The cost is that the address of an allocation is a path rather than a name, so the same instance is identified by both its position in the tree and a duplicated name inside the document title. Any move — say, the same protocol deployed on a second chain — creates a new branch rather than editing an existing entry.

The design also implies that suspension and archival operate on subtrees at whatever level fails: a protocol-wide problem archives a protocol node, a chain-level problem archives a chain node.
description: Pattern's Active Instances Directory nests Ethereum Mainnet above Maple above the Maple USDC Instance, so a single Primitive can hold many concurrent deployments distinguished by venue.
